chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is befitting for the owner of the calamity (bereaved) that he should place down his cloak until the people know that he is the owner of the calamity.

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْمُصِيبَةِ: The bereaved person / owner of the calamity

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for a bereaved person regarding their clothing in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* emphasizes the social responsibility of the bereaved to visibly signal their state of grief, thereby inviting communal support and condolences. The act of lowering the *rida'* (outer cloak) serves as a dignified, non-verbal cue that distinguishes the mourner, ensuring that the community fulfills its duty of *ta'ziyah* (consolation) effectively.
